Q1.text: This survey will help understand your healthcare needs and ensure your community has supplies like medicine, delivery packs, sanitary pads, contraceptives and free treatment during flooding. Your answers are private. Can we start?

Q2.text: What is the name of your state and community?

Q7.text: What is your annual range of income?

Q8.text: What type of living condition do you have?

Q10.text: Do you have any disability? If yes, please state.

Q11.text: Have you noticed any of these symptoms lately? Select all that apply.

options.discharge: Unusual discharge or smell from private parts

Q12.text: How long have these symptoms been happening?

Q13.text: Are the symptoms getting worse, staying the same, or improving?

Q14.text: When was the last time you had a blood test for HIV or other infections?

Q15.text: Have you had a sexual partner in the last one year?

Q16.text: How often are you able to use a condom?

Q17.text: Recently, has anyone forced or pressured you to have sex when you did not want to?

Q18.text: Have you had to exchange sex for money, food, gifts, or a place to stay?

Q19.text: Does your sexual partner have other partners, or any health problems you know about?

Q20.text: Are you currently using any method to prevent STIs (Sexually Transmitted Infections — diseases passed through sexual contact) or pregnancy?

options.want_but_no_access: I would like to but I don't have

Q21.text: Which prevention method are you using? Select all that apply.

Q23.text: How many months pregnant are you?

Q24.text: When was the last time you went for antenatal care (check-ups during pregnancy) during this pregnancy?

Q25.text: What prevents you from attending antenatal care (pregnancy check-ups)?

Q26.text: Have you experienced any of these in this pregnancy or past pregnancies? Select all that apply.

options.swelling: Swelling in feet, hands, or face

Q27.text: How old were you when you had your first pregnancy?

Q28.text: What is the time gap between each of your children?

options.over_2_years: >2 years or I have only one child

Q29.text: If pregnant now, where do you plan to deliver your baby?

Q30.text: Are you preparing for delivery and do you have a delivery pack ready? (Soap, gloves, wrapper, baby clothes, cap, socks, towel, delivery pad)

Q31.text: Where did you deliver your previous babies?

Q32.text: Have you ever had a miscarriage (lost a pregnancy before the baby was born)?

Q33.text: If yes, how many miscarriages have you had?

Q34.text: Which groups face the greatest health risks related to sexual and reproductive health during flooding? Select all that apply.

Q35.text: During floods, which of the following is available in temporary shelters? Select all that apply.

Q36.text: During flooding, are there reports of GBV (Gender-Based Violence — physical, sexual, or emotional harm based on someone's gender) in your community?

Q37.text: Which of the following are available at the health centre in your community? Select all that apply.

Q38.text: Is the health centre close enough for you to reach easily?

Q39.text: During flooding, can you still get to the nearest health centre, or are the roads flooded?

options.yes: Yes, I can access health centre

Q40.text: Were there medicines and drugs available during past floods?

Q41.text: If you have children under 5 years old, have any of them missed their vaccinations recently due to flooding?

options.up_to_date: No, they are up to date

Q42.text: Can you get help or medicine within 3 days after a sexual assault? (To prevent HIV, STIs (Sexually Transmitted Infections), or pregnancy)

Q43.text: Are warnings sent ahead of time before flooding occurs in your area?

Q44.text: Please provide your phone or WhatsApp number so that relief teams can reach you with supplies or emergency health support during the floods. (Optional)

Q45.text: Is it okay to use your anonymous answers (no name) to tell relief teams to bring supplies and more doctors and nurses to your community before the floods?

PS1.text: How easy to understand were the questions asked?

PS2.text: How well did the words used to describe specific illnesses, symptoms, or body parts match what people actually call them in this community?

PS3.text: How well did the questions asked in this survey (and the options provided) reflect the reality in the area and health problems that actually worry you, your family and the community as a whole, the most?

PS4.text: Do you have any other suggestions to make this survey better or capture the community's health reality more accurately?

PS5.text: Are there any health issues or local context that this survey missed entirely?
